subject: Consumption to Reserve realignment and short-term top-up for BrightPath
messages:
From: Jonathan Li <jonathan@brightpath.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-06-10T14:05:00Z
Subject: Sudden weekly token surge — options to avoid throttles?

Neha,

Quick heads-up: over the last 7 days our inference token consumption spiked ~3.4x from our baseline (see attached snapshot). The app hit soft-rate limits twice and several short requests timed out during peak windows (late PST afternoons). We expect this pattern to continue for at least 6–8 weeks while a new feature ramps.

We have a renewal conversation coming up in July and want to avoid impacting customers while the team finalizes the commit. What are the pragmatic paths to keep latency and throughput stable in the near term? Can we get a short-term top-up tranche or a temporary burst pool while we evaluate commit increases?

Attachment: bp-usage-metrics-202606.xlsx (Excel, ~120KB)

--
Jonathan Li
Director of ML Platform | BrightPath
jonathan@brightpath.ai
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jonathan Li <jonathan@brightpath.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-06-11T09:17:00Z
Subject: Re: Sudden weekly token surge — options to avoid throttles?

Thanks for the signal, Jonathan — sorry you hit those timeouts. I reviewed the attached usage sheet and looped in Ben (capacity) and Grace (account exec) to propose a pragmatic path. High-level options below, with immediate next steps.

1) Short-term burst tranche (recommended immediate mitigation)
   - Add a 2-week burst pool of 24 A100-equivalent GPUs (dedicated burst) to smooth peak windows.
   - No long-term commit required; billed at a higher tranche rate. Can be provisioned in ~72 hours after PO.

2) Staged commit amendment (recommended for July renewal)
   - Formalize an incremental commit increase of +30% (three-month ramp). Includes SLA uplift and priority capacity routing.
   - Requires updated contract addendum; procurement and finance sign-off.

3) Autoscale + cache tuning (software mitigations)
   - We can enable aggressive KV-prefix caching on your most frequent sessions and nudge batch thresholds to reduce token-per-request cost. Low lift, limited spike protection.

Immediate ask from our side: can you confirm the primary spike windows (local time) and the expected run length for the feature rollout? If you want to proceed with the burst tranche, please have procurement send a PO to procurement@redwoodinference.com — we'll provision on receipt and send an interim quote. I've attached a short quote for the top-up option.

Attachments: redwood-topup-options-quote.pdf

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise Lead, Renewals & Expansion
Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-06-12T16:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Consumption to Reserve realignment — capacity & provisioning notes

Neha / Grace — internal notes for provisioning and pricing calculus. Copying Jordan for SLA/runbook.

Summary of engineering impact after quick sim:
- Observed 7-day peak sustained for 6 hrs/day. Baseline utilization on existing dedicated fleet ~62% (30-day average).
- To avoid queueing during peaks we need an additional steady-state equivalent of ~18 A100 GPUs, or a short-term 24-GPU burst pool sized for concurrency and headroom.

Provisioning options and lead times:
A) Burst tranche: 24 A100-eq (ephemeral pool) — provision in ~72 hours. Reclaimable after 14 days.
B) Commit addendum: +18 A100-eq permanent reserve — provisioning staggered over 10 business days (to keep scheduler stable). Includes modification to billing profile and an updated utilization baseline for future right-sizing.

Unit economics (approx):
- Burst tranche per-GPU rate: +28% vs committed unit price.
- Commit addendum blended price: +8% vs current committed unit price (with 12-month amortization).

Operational considerations:
- If BrightPath signs PO for burst now, we’ll activate prefix-KV caching suggestions and bump concurrency limits in the same maintenance window to capture immediate benefit.
- For a commit increase, recommend a 60% utilization floor to avoid under-commit risk; we can include a 90-day lookback clause for reprofile if utilization drops.

Next steps I recommend: (1) provision burst immediately on PO to stop throttles; (2) in parallel, put together a July renewal amendment that converts a portion of the burst to commit if the new feature sustains traffic.

Ben Carter
Head of Dedicated Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Jonathan Li <jonathan@brightpath.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@brightpath.ai
Date: 2026-06-16T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Consumption to Reserve realignment and short-term top-up for BrightPath

Thanks — that plan makes sense. Procurement has approved a short-term purchase for the burst tranche while the engineering team monitors the feature for 4 weeks. Attached is the PO (PO# 6116). Can you confirm provisioning ETA and a contact for any provisioning/ops escalations?

We also want the staged conversion path documented so we can include it in our internal release notes. Happy to sign the amendment if the 30% commit increase pricing and the 90-day lookback clause are in the draft.

Attachment: BP_PO_6116.pdf (PDF, 45KB)

--
Jonathan Li
Director of ML Platform | BrightPath
